pictures.title: Webb’s First Deep Field
pictures.about: The galaxy cluster SMACS 0723, 4.6 billion light-years away, in a patch of sky the size of a grain of sand held at arm’s length. The cluster’s mass bends the light of far older galaxies behind it into arcs. Webb’s first full-colour picture, from 12.5 hours of exposure.
pictures.alt: Thousands of galaxies on a black sky, some stretched into thin orange arcs around a cluster of pale galaxies, with a few bright stars showing eight spikes.

pictures.title: The Cosmic Cliffs in Carina
pictures.about: The edge of a young star-forming region, NGC 3324, in the Carina Nebula, about 7,600 light-years away. The light and winds of hot stars above the frame carve the cloud; its tallest peaks are about 7 light-years high. Infrared light shows stars the dust hides in visible light.
pictures.alt: A ragged orange-brown wall of gas and dust like a mountain range, under a deep blue sky full of stars.

pictures.title: The Southern Ring Nebula
pictures.about: NGC 3132, about 2,500 light-years away: shells of gas and dust thrown off by a dying star, here in near-infrared light. Of the two stars at its centre, the fainter made the nebula; Webb’s mid-infrared camera showed it for the first time, wrapped in dust.
pictures.alt: An oval nebula, pale blue within ragged rings of orange, a bright star at its centre, on a black sky.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, and the Webb ERO Production Team

pictures.title: Stephan’s Quintet
pictures.about: Five galaxies close together on the sky. Four, about 290 million light-years away, pull at one another, trailing tails of gas and stars and driving a shock wave through the group; the fifth, on the left, is far nearer, at 40 million. A mosaic of more than 150 million pixels.
pictures.alt: Five galaxies, four of them tangled together with red and gold clouds between them, against many faint distant galaxies.

pictures.title: The Pillars of Creation
pictures.about: Columns of cool gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula, 6,500 light-years away, made famous by Hubble in 1995. In near-infrared light the pillars turn half transparent, and the newborn stars at their edges show: the red glow at their tips is from stars still forming.
pictures.alt: Three tall brown and orange columns of dust rising against a blue field crowded with stars.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; J. DePasquale, A. Koekemoer, A. Pagan (STScI)

pictures.title: The heart of the Phantom Galaxy
pictures.about: The spiral galaxy M74, about 32 million light-years away in Pisces, seen face on in mid-infrared light. Filaments of gas and dust wind out along its arms, and its centre, clear of gas, shows the cluster of stars at its core.
pictures.alt: A spiral of fine grey and white filaments winding around a bright blue centre.
pictures.credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, J. Lee and the PHANGS-JWST Team. Acknowledgement: J. Schmidt

pictures.title: The Cartwheel Galaxy
pictures.about: A galaxy about 500 million light-years away in Sculptor, with two smaller companions. A smaller galaxy passed through its middle, and two rings spread from the collision like ripples on a pond; the outer ring has been growing for about 440 million years, forming stars as it goes.
pictures.alt: A galaxy like a wheel, a bright hub joined by red spokes to a pink and blue rim, with two small galaxies to its left.

pictures.title: Neptune and its rings
pictures.about: Neptune in near-infrared light, where it is not blue: methane in its air absorbs that light, and only its high clouds of methane ice shine. The clearest view of its rings since Voyager 2 flew past in 1989.
pictures.alt: A pale glowing globe with bright streaks of cloud, circled by thin faint rings and a few small moons.

pictures.title: The Hubble Ultra Deep Field
pictures.about: Nearly 10,000 galaxies in a patch of sky in Fornax a tenth as wide as the full Moon, from about a million seconds of exposure over 400 orbits in 2003 and 2004. The faintest and reddest are seen as they were when the universe was less than a billion years old.
pictures.alt: A black sky crowded with small galaxies of every shape, white, blue, orange and red, the smallest only faint specks.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, and S. Beckwith (STScI) and the HUDF Team

pictures.title: The Pillars of Creation
pictures.about: Columns of cold gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula (M16), about 6,500 light-years away, the tallest some four light-years high. Stars form inside them while the light of young stars nearby wears them away. Hubble first pictured them in 1995; this sharper, wider view in visible light was taken in 2014.
pictures.alt: Three dark brown towers of dust with glowing edges, rising against a blue-green haze and a few bright stars.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA/Hubble and the Hubble Heritage Team

pictures.title: The Orion Nebula
pictures.about: The nearest large region where stars are being born, about 1,500 light-years away, with more than 3,000 stars in view. The four massive stars of the Trapezium, at its bright heart, have hollowed out the cloud with their light. A mosaic taken over 105 orbits.
pictures.alt: Billowing clouds of pink, red and brown gas around a bright white hollow, sprinkled with stars.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, M. Robberto (Space Telescope Science Institute/ESA) and the Hubble Space Telescope Orion Treasury Project Team

pictures.title: The Crab Nebula
pictures.about: What is left of a star whose explosion Chinese and Japanese astronomers recorded in 1054: threads of gas six light-years across, still flying outward, and at the centre a neutron star turning 30 times a second. About 6,500 light-years away; a mosaic of 24 exposures.
pictures.alt: An oval cloud of tangled orange and green threads around a blue-white glow, on a black sky.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA and Allison Loll/Jeff Hester (Arizona State University). Acknowledgement: Davide De Martin (ESA/Hubble)

pictures.title: The Whirlpool Galaxy
pictures.about: The spiral galaxy M51 and its small companion NGC 5195, about 31 million light-years away. The companion’s pull, as it passes behind, is thought to sharpen the spiral arms, pink where new stars are forming. Released for Hubble’s fifteenth year in orbit.
pictures.alt: A face-on spiral galaxy with two long arms dotted pink and blue, one arm reaching to a smaller yellow galaxy at the right.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, S. Beckwith (STScI), and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

pictures.title: The Sombrero Galaxy
pictures.about: The galaxy M104 seen almost edge-on, about 28 million light-years away and 50,000 light-years across: a bright bulge of old stars crossed by a dark lane of dust. A mosaic of six pictures taken in 2003.
pictures.alt: A glowing white disc seen from the side, like a wide-brimmed hat, with a dark band of dust along its rim.
pictures.credit: NASA/ESA and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

pictures.title: The Butterfly Nebula
pictures.about: NGC 6302, about 3,800 light-years away in Scorpius: gas thrown off by a dying star once about five times the Sun’s mass, in two lobes more than two light-years from tip to tip. The star hides behind a ring of dust at the waist. Among the first pictures from the camera astronauts fitted in May 2009.
pictures.alt: Two ragged wings of pink, white and orange gas spreading from a narrow dark waist, on a black sky.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble SM4 ERO Team

pictures.title: Mystic Mountain
pictures.about: A pillar of gas and dust three light-years tall in the Carina Nebula, about 7,500 light-years away, worn by the light of nearby stars. Jets of gas shoot from young stars hidden in its peaks. Released for Hubble’s twentieth year in orbit.
pictures.alt: A craggy brown and gold tower of dust with wisps streaming from its top, against blue and orange haze.
pictures.credit: NASA, ESA, M. Livio and the Hubble 20th Anniversary Team (STScI)
